You won't always have to use the phone....

Last week, the government announced that it was IMPOSING its new contract on general practice. We will no longer be able to cap our online consultations. We will  have to take GPs away from seeing patients to respond to, and medically triage, the online "tickets". 

Of course, that means there will be fewer actual appointments and consequently whilst your access will improve, the capacity to see you will be reduced yet further. The result will be that we will be left with no choice but introduce waiting lists in general practice.

Still, you'll be able to plan your life. 

And if you have time check this out....

Thank you for highlighting how much pressure GP surgeries are currently under.
Some of the reasons can be explained here:

https://youtu.be/s_s4GJacPRk?si=zCpcNmieLV9gvvqq

If you remain unhappy with our services you have 4 options:

1. Register with a neighbouring GP practice. However as we now work at Network levels you will still have the same Urgent Care Service whichever practice you are with.

2. To avoid the situation above you would need to move out of the catchment area e.g. Totton or Lymington so of course that is not practical at all.

3. Support General Practice and voice your concerns to the local MP. It’s the government who decide on our funding and force the rules on us that we have to work by, so rather than hearing the voice of a GP practice, why don’t you as a voter make yourself heard?

4. Do nothing. Moan on Google reviews, Facebook forums and the like. Feel better for it. Fail to understand that hard working GP practices are doing the best they can for their patients. Allow apathy to set in and accept that there will be no change unless you, the voting public,  call the politicians out.

Anyway. After about 20 mins if someone has not checked-in it registers with the clinician as a non-attendance. 
Every clinician still comes out and calls a patient in if we are aware that they’re in the waiting room.
